newsitem.title: USA: Phar-Mor, Shopko combining under new holding company.
newsitem.headline: Phar-Mor, Shopko combining under new holding company.

text.p: Phar-Mor Inc. and ShopKo Inc. said Monday they agreed to merge, forming a new holding company for the two drugstore retailers.
They said the new entity, to be called Cabot Noble Inc., is expected to have combined annual sales of about $3.2 billion from 232 stores in 29 states.
ShopKo and Phar-Mor will continue as separate operating subsidiaries of Cabot Noble.

Robert Haft, current chairman and CEO of Phar-Mor, will be chairman and CEO of Cabot Noble. David Schwartz will remain president of Youngstown, Ohio-based Phar-Mor and Dale Kramer will remain president and CEO of ShopKo, based in Green Bay, Wis.
ShopKo has 130 stores in 15 states, primarily in the Midwest, Pacific Northwest, and Mountain regions. Phar-Mor has 102 stores in 18 states, primarily in Ohio, Pennsylvania, and Virginia.
The companies valued the deal, which involves a three-way exchange of shares, at approximately $1 billion, including the assumption of debt.
About two-thirds of the two companies' sales is in similar merchandise categories, particularly in the area of pharmacy, health and beauty aids, and general merchandise.
They said the combined operations will realise potential annual savings of approximately $15 million to $20 million.

Based on current sales figures, the companies will have nearly $500 million of combined annual pharmacy sales, an additional $500 million of sales in drug store-related products, and approximately $1 billion in general merchandise sales.
The remaining $1 billion in combined new company sales includes revenues from ShopKo's ProVantage, Inc., health care subsidiary and other merchandise areas that the companies do not now share.

Under the share exchanges, each share of ShopKo common stock will be exchanged for 2.4 shares of Cabot Noble stock, which may be adjusted if the value falls outside a range of $17.25 to $18.00 per share based on the average daily closing prices of Phar-Mor shares over a specified 30-day time period.
Each share of Phar-Mor common stock will be exchanged for one share of Cabot Noble stock.
ShopKo's stock closed Friday at $16.25 on the New York Stock Exchange. Phar-Mor ended Friday at $8.125 on Nasdaq.

After the share exchanges are completed, Supervalu Inc., which owns 46 percent of ShopKo, will sell the Cabot Noble common stock it receives to Cabot Noble for a total purchase price of about $248.4 million.

The exchange will involve about $208 million in cash and $40.4 million in a short-term note maturing Jan. 31, 1997, the company said, representing a purchase price of $16.86 per share of ShopKo held by Supervalu prior to the share exchange.
At the Sept. 6, 1996 closing price of $16.25 for ShopKo, the value of the share exchange represents a 6 percent to 11 percent premium for the ShopKo shares.

After the repurchase of Cabot Noble shares from Supervalu, the ShopKo public shareholders will hold approximately 77 percent of the combined company, compared with their current 54 percent ownership of ShopKo.
Cabot Noble intends to file for listing on the New York Stock Exchange.
